conclusion.justification: The report explicitly states that the evidence does not support the claim that CoQ10 improves movement symptoms in Parkinson's disease, citing a definitive Phase III trial that refuted earlier positive signals and concluding that the answer appears to be no.
conclusion.label: rejects

report:
I researched this, and the evidence does **not** support the claim that CoQ10 improves movement symptoms in Parkinson's disease — in fact, the most rigorous evidence points the other way.

**Early, smaller trials suggested possible benefit.** A Phase II trial testing CoQ10 at 300, 600, and 1200 mg/day in early, untreated PD patients found it safe and well-tolerated, with results suggesting it "may slow the progressive impairment of PD" as measured by the UPDRS ([jamanetwork.com](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaneurology/fullarticle/782965); [ninds.nih.gov](https://www.ninds.nih.gov/health-information/clinical-trials/effects-coenzyme-q10-coq-parkinson-disease)). The original study authors themselves cautioned these results "need to be confirmed in a larger study."

**The larger, definitive Phase III trial refuted this.** A subsequent randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind Phase III trial (Beal et al.) tested high-dosage CoQ10 in early PD specifically to confirm the earlier signal. It found that CoQ10 "does not slow the progression of Parkinson's disease" and showed no clinical benefit ([jamanetwork.com](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaneurology/fullarticle/1851409)). This was widely reported as CoQ10 "striking out" in Phase 3 testing ([alzforum.org](https://www.alzforum.org/news/research-news/coenzyme-q10-strikes-out-phase-3-parkinsons)).

**A recent systematic review** on CoQ10 in Parkinsonian syndromes similarly notes CoQ10's theoretical antioxidant rationale (given mitochondrial dysfunction/oxidative stress in PD pathogenesis) but does not establish it as an effective treatment for motor symptoms.

**Conclusion:** The current best evidence, especially the larger, more rigorous Phase III RCT, contradicts the idea that CoQ10 improves movement disorders in PD. Early positive signals from smaller trials were not replicated. I'd revise the original assumption — the answer appears to be **no**.
